title: Quantum skyrmion parallelism via metasurface-tailored high-dimensional entanglement
authors: Pedro Ornelas, Ramona Bedford, Fazilah Nothlawala, Chi Li, Haoyi Yu, Isaac Nape, Stefan A. Maier, Haoran Ren, Andrew Forbes
abstract: Quantum skyrmions are topological structures that have garnered significant interest due to their demonstrated robustness and versatility across diverse optical platforms. However, existing approaches for their generation are limited to producing pre-determined two dimensional qubit states with a single topology. Here we create multi-dimensional topological states by introducing a non-local interaction between high-dimensional photonic entanglement and a metasurface, where the topological transformation induced by the metasurface is made non-deterministic by the probabilistic nature of the interfacing entangled state. Within this framework, we demonstrate that individual quantum states can host multiple co-existing topologies that are only revealed upon measurement, allowing for their parallel transport within distinct spatial mode channels. We confirm this by revealing the rich topological landscape within our modified Hilbert space while controlling the desired output topology by orbital angular momentum (OAM) projections on one of the entangled photons, producing multiple non-local polarization-OAM entangled states characterized by distinct topological classes, all from a single metasurface device. Our results reveal new capability when structured high-dimensional entanglement is interfaced with structured matter capable of coupling photonic degrees of freedom, establishing a new pathway for the compact generation of complex quantum states.
summary: This paper presents a novel method to generate multiple, distinct quantum skyrmion topologies simultaneously from a single metasurface device. By coupling high-dimensional photonic entanglement (OAM-OAM pairs) to a structured metasurface, the authors overcome the limitation of single-topology generation. This establishes a new, compact pathway for engineering complex quantum states for quantum information applications.
main_problem: Existing methods for generating quantum skyrmions are limited to producing pre-determined two-dimensional qubit states with a single topology.
main_result: The authors demonstrated the compact generation of multiple, distinct topological quantum states from a single metasurface device by interfacing it with high-dimensional photonic entanglement.
method: The approach uses a metasurface to induce a non-local, probabilistic topological transformation on a high-dimensional OAM-OAM entangled photonic state.
model_or_system: The system utilizes quantum skyrmions realized in optical platforms, specifically employing biphoton entanglement generated via SPDC and interacting with a metasurface (J-plate) designed with amorphous silicon nanopillars.
key_observables: Topological winding number (N), Concurrence (C), Purity ($\gamma$), and Fidelity (F) are used to characterize the generated states and their entanglement.
important_parameters: The topological control is achieved by varying parameters $(m, n)$ related to the metasurface transformation, yielding multiple distinct topological classes.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the ability to characterize the joint state correlation structure and the assumption that the metasurface interaction can be modeled to induce controlled topological shifts.
figures_summary: Figures compare the proposed scheme (biphoton HD entanglement $ightarrow$ multiple topologies) against single-photon methods, and show the metasurface design and resulting shifted OAM spiral bandwidth.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the limitation of single-topology generation to proposing the metasurface-entanglement interface, detailing the physical implementation using OAM-OAM entangled pairs, and finally quantifying the resulting multi-topological states using various quantum metrics.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the generation and control of complex topological quantum states using structured light and engineered matter, which is highly relevant to quantum optics and photonic quantum information processing.
